commit_message:
[wasm] Introduce TypeNamesProvider for canonical types

As part of our quest to use CanonicalValueTypes more, we need the
ability to print them for debugging. This CL adds the required
infrastructure; uses of it will follow.

findings.title: Debug-only type-kind check in TypeCanonicalizer::LookupStruct (and friends) allows sandbox type confusion
findings.message: TypeCanonicalizer::LookupStruct, LookupArray, and LookupFunctionSignature are called with untrusted canonical type indices sourced from sandboxed WebAssembly bytecode. After a range-bounds check (SBXCHECK), the code retrieves the CanonicalType* and then verifies its kind with DCHECK_EQ. Because DCHECK_EQ compiles to a no-op in release (non-debug) builds, an attacker who can supply an in-bounds type index that refers to a different type kind (e.g., an array-type index passed to LookupStruct) will bypass the kind check entirely. The function then reads the wrong union member (e.g., type->struct_type when the actual union payload is array_type or function_sig), resulting in a type-confused pointer being returned to the caller and ultimately allowing a V8 sandbox violation via the subsequent StructTypeBase::field access.
findings.suggestion: Replace DCHECK_EQ(type->kind, CanonicalType::kStruct) (and the equivalent checks in LookupArray and LookupFunctionSignature) with SBXCHECK(type->kind == CanonicalType::kStruct). SBXCHECK is enforced in both debug and release builds and terminates the process on failure, preventing the type-confused pointer from being returned.

ground_truth.root_cause: The Lookup* functions were introduced in commit dbb5628854a with DCHECK_EQ for the type-kind guard. DCHECK_EQ is a debug-only assertion; it is compiled to nothing in release/production builds. Because the canonical type index is attacker-controlled (it originates from untrusted WebAssembly bytecode running inside the sandbox), the missing production-time check allows the type confusion to occur. The SBXCHECK macro — which is enforced in all builds — was only applied to the range check, not to the kind check.
